solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: The two consuming starter of rich soup (5)

indicatorNotes.consuming: BOTH eats the R, so it ends up inside
indicatorNotes.starter of: the starter of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of rich, taken inside B…OTH

annotation.surface: A pair of diners polishing off the first course of a rich soup.
annotation.walkthrough: "Starter" looks like the soup course on a menu, but here it only means the first letter of "rich".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: broth is a thin soup made by simmering meat or vegetables.

entries.clue: British bird dog (6)

annotation.surface: A list of British wildlife: a bird, a dog.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bird dog" reads as a gundog that fetches birds, but the words split: "British bird" is the wordplay and "dog" alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The beagle is a small hound bred for hunting hares.

entries.clue: Very old tailor in orange coat (12)

indicatorNotes.tailor: to tailor is to cut and refashion, so the letters are reworked

annotation.surface: An elderly tailor working in a bright orange coat.
annotation.walkthrough: "Very old tailor" reads as a person, but "tailor" is a verb acting on the whole of "in orange coat", including the little word "in".
annotation.definitionFit: An octogenarian is someone in their eighties, which is very old.

entries.clue: Stern on vessel in difficulty (8)

blocks.note: placed before, in a down clue

annotation.surface: A boat in trouble, seen from its stern.
annotation.walkthrough: "Stern" and "vessel" together suggest the back of a boat; stern here is the adjective meaning strict.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hardship is a condition of suffering, one of the senses of difficulty.

entries.clue: Introductions to duke, earl, judge and viscount use sense of repetition (4,2)

indicatorNotes.Introductions to: each word's introduction is its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: duke, earl, judge and viscount use
blocks.note: first letters of the six words

annotation.surface: A formal line about how dukes, earls, judges and viscounts should be introduced.
annotation.walkthrough: "And" and "use" look like filler joining the titles, but both give letters: A and U.
annotation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the feeling that you have lived through this moment before.

entries.clue: New method to lift something boring (4)

indicatorNotes.to lift: in a down clue, lifting turns the letters bottom to top

annotation.surface: An engineer's new way of raising a drill.
annotation.walkthrough: "Boring" suggests drilling beside "lift", but it means dull; a yawn can be a tedious thing as well as the reaction to one.
annotation.definitionFit: A yawn is informal for something tedious: the meeting was a yawn.

entries.clue: Name missing from gift arranged in advance (6)

indicatorNotes.missing from: the N is absent from the gift

annotation.surface: A gift prepared ahead of time that has no name tag on it.
annotation.definitionFit: Preset means set or arranged beforehand.
annotation.walkthrough: "Name" looks like a label on the gift, but it is just the letter N to take out.

entries.clue: Work relaxed an ancient Macedonian hero (9)

indicatorNotes.Work: work the letters, as dough is worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A laid-back work ethic attributed to a classical hero.
annotation.walkthrough: "Work relaxed" reads as easygoing labour; "Work" is an instruction on "relaxed an".
annotation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the king of Macedon who conquered much of the ancient world.

entries.clue: Rude — too rude — I cuss terribly (12)

indicatorNotes.terribly: the letters are put in a terrible mess

annotation.surface: Someone admitting, mid-rant, that their swearing has gone too far.
annotation.walkthrough: The same word "rude" is both the definition and part of the fodder, and the whole surface acts out the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Discourteous means impolite, which is rude.

entries.clue: Roof support with no front behind (5)

indicatorNotes.with no front: the first letter is taken away

blocks.note: a rafter holds up a roof; drop the R

annotation.surface: A roof beam that has lost its front end.
annotation.walkthrough: "Front" and "behind" sit side by side as opposites, which disguises that "behind" is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: After can mean behind, as in following after someone.

entries.clue: Withdrawing air to help is for identification of a problem (9)

indicatorNotes.Withdrawing: drawing back, so SONG and AID run backwards

blocks.note: an air is a tune or song

annotation.surface: Pulling back ventilation help, as though for a fault report.
annotation.walkthrough: "Air" looks like breath or ventilation beside "withdrawing", but it means a tune. The reversal stops before "is", which joins on as written.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical and mechanical term: a doctor's or engineer's diagnosis is the naming of what is wrong.

entries.clue: Woman never undressed (3)

indicatorNotes.undressed: stripped of its outer layer, so the end letters come off

blocks.note: NEVER without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A woman who has never been seen undressed.
annotation.walkthrough: Eve is the woman in Eden who wore nothing at all, so the surface is literally true of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Eve is a woman's name, and the first woman in Genesis.

entries.clue: Hard time catching river snake in floating home (9)

indicatorNotes.catching: H and T catch the river and snake between them

blocks.note: the Ouse is an English river

annotation.surface: A rough spell on a houseboat when a river snake is caught.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a houseboat is a boat people live on, a home that floats.
annotation.walkthrough: "Hard time" reads as a rough spell, but it splits into two letters that wrap round the rest.

entries.clue: Put at risk, stop rage (8)

annotation.surface: A plea to calm down: anger endangers you.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to endanger someone is to expose them to harm.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma sits where a solver might expect a list; "stop rage" is two words joined into one answer.

entries.clue: Perhaps did butterfly scheme initially drain fen area? (9)

indicatorNotes.initially: only the initial letter of drain is used

blocks.note: butterfly is a swimming stroke, so someone doing it swam

annotation.surface: A question about whether a butterfly survey or a drainage scheme was carried out on the fens.
annotation.walkthrough: "Butterfly" belongs in a picture of fenland insects, but it is the swimming stroke; "Perhaps" admits that butterfly is only one way to have swum.
annotation.definitionFit: A fen is low wet ground, and swampland is an area of such marshy ground.

entries.clue: Tool for cutting diseased edges of lucerne (6)

indicatorNotes.edges of: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of lucerne

annotation.surface: A farm tool for trimming the blighted edges of a lucerne crop.
annotation.walkthrough: Lucerne is a fodder crop, also called alfalfa, so the whole surface stays in the field.
annotation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved blade for cutting grass or grain.

entries.clue: A Liberal exists? They say one’s somewhere else (6)

annotation.surface: A sceptic asking whether a Liberal really exists, since they always seem to be elsewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: "They say" wants to signal a sound-alike, but here it is plain speech: alibis are the things that claim you were elsewhere.
annotation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim that the accused was somewhere else at the time.

entries.clue: Back equality in declamatory song style (3)

indicatorNotes.Back: as an adverb, back means towards the rear, so the letters are read from the rear forwards

blocks.note: at par = equal, as in on a par with

annotation.surface: Supporting equal rights through a spoken-word protest song.
annotation.walkthrough: "Back" looks like the verb meaning support, as in backing a cause.
annotation.definitionFit: Rap is music in which the words are spoken rhythmically, a declaimed style.

entries.clue: Circle among favourite railway lines (6)

indicatorNotes.among: the O goes among the letters of PET

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

annotation.surface: A loop in the middle of a much-loved rail network.
annotation.walkthrough: "Railway lines" reads as track, but "lines" stands alone as the definition: lines of verse.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword favourite: lines means verse, as in learning your lines of a poem.

entries.clue: Requirement to fix rot in rice (9)

indicatorNotes.fix: to fix is to repair, so the letters are put right in a new order

annotation.surface: A food-safety rule demanding that mouldy rice be dealt with.
annotation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard or requirement something must meet.
annotation.walkthrough: "Requirement to fix" reads as a single job to do, but "to" is a link and "fix" works on "rot in rice".

entries.clue: Repeat fifth word of radio series (4)

blocks.note: to repeat a sound back is what a canyon wall does
the radio series is the phonetic alphabet; its fifth word stands for E

annotation.surface: A request to repeat the fifth word of a radio broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: The radio series is not a programme but the phonetic alphabet radio operators use to spell letters, where Echo stands for E.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to echo is to repeat another's words, and in the NATO alphabet the fifth code word is Echo.

entries.clue: Spirit of good party-giver (5)

annotation.surface: Praise for the generous spirit of someone who throws a good party.
annotation.walkthrough: "Spirit" reads as a quality of character, but it means a ghost.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spirit in the sense of a disembodied soul, the thing that haunts.

entries.clue: Left the cumin out when midday meal is taken (9)

indicatorNotes.out: the letters are put out of order

annotation.surface: A cook who forgot the cumin in the dish served at midday.
annotation.walkthrough: "Left out" reads as forgot, but "Left" gives L and "out" acts on the whole of L plus "the cumin".
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the phrase describes the hour of the midday meal.

entries.clue: Hazardous lead-in for Radio 1 broadcaster (5)

indicatorNotes.lead-in for: the lead-in of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: 1 looks like the Roman numeral I

annotation.surface: A dangerous introduction to a Radio 1 show.
annotation.walkthrough: "Radio 1" is a BBC station name and reads as one unit, but it splits into the R and the I.
annotation.definitionFit: Risky means involving danger, so hazardous.
